references.text: Earlier in the story, the donkey sees the angel of the Lord for the first time and turns off the road, showing the same pattern where the animal sees what Balaam cannot see.
The third time the donkey sees the angel of the Lord, she lies down under Balaam, and he strikes her again, continuing the pattern from verse 25.
The Lord opens Balaam's eyes so that he finally sees the angel whom the donkey has seen all along, including in verse 25.
Peter refers to Balaam's donkey that spoke with a human voice and stopped the prophet's madness, a direct reference to this story.
God opens Hagar's eyes so that she sees the spring of water, a similar motif where God reveals something hidden from human sight.
